issues.title: orgId parameter not propagated in getTeamIdsWithPermission
issues.description: The method getTeamIdsWithPermission accepts an orgId parameter to scope permission checks to a specific organization, but it fails to pass this parameter to the underlying getTeamIdsWithPermissions method. This causes organization scoping to be ignored when checking single permissions, allowing users to potentially access teams from all organizations instead of only the specified one. The bug breaks the core security feature introduced in this PR where organization-scoped permission checks were meant to restrict access based on orgId.

issues.title: Incomplete orgId filtering in PBAC child team query
issues.description: In the SQL query for getTeamsWithPBACPermissions, the WHERE clause for child teams is missing a check for child."parentId" = ${orgId}. The original PR added this condition to properly scope child teams when an orgId is provided, but this implementation only checks org."id" and child."id", missing the case where a child team's parent should match the orgId. This causes the query to incorrectly exclude child teams whose parentId matches the specified orgId, breaking the inheritance model where organization permissions should propagate to child teams.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
SELECT DISTINCT child."id"
FROM "Membership" m
INNER JOIN "Role" r ON m."customRoleId" = r.id
INNER JOIN "Team" org ON m."teamId" = org.id
INNER JOIN "Team" child ON child."parentId" = org.id
WHERE m."userId" = ${userId}
  AND m."accepted" = true
  AND m."customRoleId" IS NOT NULL
  AND (${orgId}::bigint IS NULL OR org."id" = ${orgId} OR child."id" = ${orgId})

issues.title: Authorization bypass when filtering multiple userIds including current user
issues.description: The isCurrentUser check was changed from a strict equality check (filters.userIds.length === 1 && user.id === filters.userIds[0]) to a loose inclusion check (filters.userIds.includes(user.id)). This allows a user to bypass permission checks by including their own userId in a list alongside other userIds they don't have permission to access. For example, if a user requests bookings for [ownUserId, unauthorizedUserId], the check passes even though they lack permission for the unauthorized user, allowing them to access bookings they shouldn't see.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #25434 - fix: get bookings handler for pbac and fallback roles

structured_output.summary:
The PR moves the bookings `getBookings` handler off direct ADMIN/OWNER membership queries and onto `PermissionCheckService.getTeamIdsWithPermission("booking.read")`, so PBAC custom roles and fallback roles both grant booking visibility. It also threads an optional `orgId` through the service, repository interface, and both raw SQL queries in `PermissionRepository`, and replaces the membership-based user and event-type lookups with team-ID based ones. The PBAC/fallback refactor is a reasonable direction and the parallel-query structure is kept.

However, I found a critical authorization regression in the handler. The `isCurrentUser` check was loosened from "the filter is exactly [self]" to "the filter contains self", which lets a caller bypass the FORBIDDEN guard by padding `userIds` with their own ID. Separately, `orgId` is accepted by the service and interface but silently dropped by the `getTeamIdsWithPermission` wrapper in `PermissionRepository`, so the handler's org scoping never reaches SQL. The integration tests call the repository directly and therefore miss this, and the handler tests use weak `.resolves.not.toThrow()` assertions that cannot catch either problem.
structured_output.verdictRationale: A critical authorization bypass is introduced: `isCurrentUser` now returns true for any filter that contains the caller's own ID, so `userIds: [self, victimId]` skips the FORBIDDEN check and returns the victim's bookings. The `orgId` scoping the PR advertises is also not applied on the production path because the repository's single-permission wrapper drops it. Both must be fixed before merge; the test and lint issues are secondary.

architecture.overview:
Before this PR, `getBookings` in `get.handler.ts` built its visibility scope by querying `Membership` rows with role ADMIN/OWNER, optionally narrowed to `user.orgId`, and then used those membership IDs to find event types, users, and emails. Anything PBAC-based (custom roles) was invisible to this path. `PermissionCheckService` and `PermissionRepository` already computed the set of team IDs a user holds a permission on, combining PBAC custom roles with fallback roles for teams that have PBAC disabled, including child teams reached through an org membership.

The PR routes the handler through that service. It asks for team IDs with `booking.read`, then derives event-type IDs and user IDs/emails from those teams. It also adds an optional `orgId` to the service, interface, and SQL so results can be scoped to an organization. The org scope is supposed to be applied in the repository's SQL, but as written the top-level single-permission wrapper does not forward it, and the handler's `userIds` guard was loosened in a way that bypasses the FORBIDDEN check.
steps: Entry point: the `viewer.bookings.get` tRPC procedure calls `getHandler`, which builds `user.orgId` from `profile.organizationId` and passes it into `getBookings`.

Permission lookup (changed): `getBookings` now constructs `PermissionCheckService` and calls `getTeamIdsWithPermission({ permission: "booking.read", fallbackRoles: [ADMIN, OWNER], orgId })`. The service validates the permission and forwards the call to `PermissionRepository`.

Repository SQL (changed): `getTeamIdsWithPermissions` runs two queries in parallel. One covers custom-role PBAC memberships and the other covers fallback-role memberships on teams without the PBAC feature flag. Each has an `orgId` predicate that is skipped when `orgId` is NULL. The single-permission wrapper at line 222 is the broken link.

Team to scope expansion (changed): the returned team IDs feed `getEventTypeIdsFromTeamIdsFilter` (event types of those teams plus managed children of parents) and `getUserIdsAndEmailsFromTeamIds` (members of those teams), replacing the old membership-condition helpers.

Userids guard (changed, risky): `getBookings` validates explicit `filters.userIds` against the accessible user set, with an `isCurrentUser` escape hatch. That escape hatch now accepts any list containing the caller, which is the bypass.
Booking union: the accessible user IDs, emails, and event-type IDs are used to build the Kysely union queries (steps 1–7). The union is unchanged apart from renamed variables.

findings.title: isCurrentUser bypass exposes other users' bookings
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/get.handler.ts`, the `isCurrentUser` check (around line 149) was loosened to `filters.userIds.includes(user.id)`, which lets a caller bypass the FORBIDDEN guard (lines 146-156) by adding their own ID to a list that also contains out-of-scope users. Change the guard so every requested userId must either equal `user.id` or be in `allAccessibleUserIds`. Do not allow a mixed list to pass. Restoring the original exact-match behavior is also acceptable. Add a unit test in `get.handler.test.ts` for `userIds: [self, outsiderId]` that expects FORBIDDEN.

findings.title: orgId dropped by single-permission repository wrapper
findings.body:
`PermissionRepository.getTeamIdsWithPermission` accepts `orgId` and the interface declares it, but the call at line 222 omits it. The service forwards `orgId` to the repository, so the scope is lost on the production path used by the bookings handler.

::diff{file="packages/features/pbac/infrastructure/repositories/PermissionRepository.ts" lines="211-222"}

Failure scenario: an org admin with `orgId` set calls the bookings list. `getTeamIdsWithPermission` ignores `orgId`, so teams from other organizations and standalone teams where the caller is ADMIN/OWNER are included. This is a regression from the base code, which restricted the membership scope to `user.orgId`. The integration tests pass only because they call `getTeamIdsWithPermissions` (plural) directly, which does honor `orgId`.

The same wrapper pattern exists for the single-permission path in `getTeamIdsWithPermission` and should forward `orgId` the same way.
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/pbac/infrastructure/repositories/PermissionRepository.ts`, `getTeamIdsWithPermission` (around line 222) accepts `orgId` but calls `this.getTeamIdsWithPermissions({ userId, permissions: [permission], fallbackRoles })` without it, so org scoping is silently dropped for the bookings handler. Forward `orgId` into that call. Then add an integration or handler-level test that calls the service path (`PermissionCheckService.getTeamIdsWithPermission` with `orgId`) and asserts teams from another org are excluded, since the existing tests only hit the plural repository method.

findings.title: Handler tests assert nothing about results or the bypass
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/get.handler.test.ts`, replace the `.resolves.not.toThrow()` assertions (around lines 277, 299, and 333) with assertions on observable outcomes, such as the returned bookings or the Kysely/prisma calls with the expected user IDs and emails. Add a case for `userIds: [self, outsiderId]` that expects a FORBIDDEN error. Add a case that asserts `mockGetTeamIdsWithPermission` receives `orgId` when `user.orgId` is set, using `mockUser` with a non-null `orgId`.

findings.title: Unused TRPCError import in permission-check service
findings.body:
`TRPCError` is imported at line 6 of `permission-check.service.ts` but is never used in the file. Lint rules for unused imports will fail the build, and the import also couples this domain service to tRPC.

::diff{file="packages/features/pbac/services/permission-check.service.ts" lines="5-8"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/pbac/services/permission-check.service.ts`, remove the unused `import { TRPCError } from "@trpc/server";` on line 6. Confirm nothing else in that file references `TRPCError`, and make sure lint passes.

findings.title: Unused TRPCError import in handler test
findings.body:
`get.handler.test.ts` imports `TRPCError` on line 5, but the file never references it. The FORBIDDEN assertions use `rejects.toMatchObject` on the error code and message instead.

::diff{file="packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/get.handler.test.ts" lines="1-6"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/get.handler.test.ts`, remove the unused `import { TRPCError } from "@trpc/server";` on line 5 and confirm the file still passes lint.

findings.title: Inconsistent orgId predicates between PBAC and fallback child-team queries
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/pbac/infrastructure/repositories/PermissionRepository.ts`, the fallback child-team branch (around line 357) has a redundant `child."parentId" = ${orgId}` predicate, while the PBAC child-team branch (around line 309) does not. Make both child branches use the same orgId predicate, dropping the redundant `child.parentId` clause, and keep the direct-team branches consistent with each other.

findings.title: Unrelated whitespace and reformat churn in permission-check service
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/pbac/services/permission-check.service.ts`, revert the formatting-only edits that are unrelated to the `orgId` change: the trailing-whitespace removals around lines 139 and 203, and the `getHighestRole` signature collapse at line 297. Keep only the `TRPCError` import removal and the `orgId` changes.

findings.title: Permission lookup errors are swallowed and return an empty scope
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/get.handler.ts` (around lines 117-122), `getTeamIdsWithPermission` from `PermissionCheckService` swallows all errors and returns `[]`, so a failing permission query silently narrows the bookings scope to the caller's own bookings. Either call the repository path in a way that surfaces the error for this handler, or wrap the call so that failures are logged at error level and rethrown as an internal error. Do not change other callers of the service.

findings.title: PBAC and fallback orgId scoping via the team-to-org hierarchy
findings.body:
The reworked `PermissionRepository` SQL reuses one shape for both PBAC and fallback roles. Each query uses a direct-team branch and a child-team branch via `org.id` joins, with `orgId` checked in both. The new integration tests cover the org-level filter and child-team inclusion, which is useful coverage for the repository.

The design also keeps the parallel PBAC and fallback queries and merges them in code. That keeps the existing `getTeamIdsWithPermissions` contract and avoids a larger SQL rewrite.

findings.title: Event-type scope keeps managed-parent coverage
findings.body:
The old `getEventTypeIdsWhereUserIsAdminOrOwner` included child event types of managed parents through `parent.team`. The new `getEventTypeIdsFromTeamIdsFilter` keeps the same parent-team branch, so reusing it for the permission-derived team IDs preserves that coverage without a separate helper.
